next_changelog: Added concrete positional rules to [When to Segment] for boundary types the critic showed are safe but missing: leading standalone discourse connectives (그니까/그래서/근데/아니), trailing self-contained rhetorical tag-questions, embedded question marks followed by a summarizing clause, coordinated self-contained -고 clauses, internal temporal connectives (그러고 나서/그 다음에), leading filler-interjection clusters, and placing the boundary after the main verb phrase in filler-laden run-ons rather than leaving them whole.

Extended [Decision Procedure] with two repositioning checks: (a) if clause B's subject is only introduced right after a candidate boundary, shift the boundary to fall after that subject phrase instead of before it, and (b) for a single cause-then-result chain (e.g. -아서/-가지고 reason clause immediately followed by its result), use one boundary around the whole chain rather than multiple internal cuts, so the causal/result link is not severed. These reposition existing boundaries per the 'move boundaries, keep the count' direction and do not add new prohibitions or reduce split frequency.

next_changelog: Added three narrowly-scoped, low-risk positional rules to [When to Segment] that were shown safe by the critic's reference evidence: (1) segment right after a leading standalone discourse connective (그니까/그래서/근데/아니/그런데) when a full subject+predicate clause follows it, (2) explicitly extend the existing terminal-punctuation rule to embedded mid-sentence '?' followed by a summarizing clause, not just sentence-final '?', (3) segment immediately before an internal temporal connective (그러고 나서, 그 다음에) that introduces a second, distinct describable time span. These reposition/add boundaries without touching the -고 coordination wording, tag-question splitting, or filler-cluster splitting that were part of the previously rejected revision and likely caused its quality collapse.

Added a preliminary check to [Decision Procedure] step 1 requiring the three new [When to Segment] patterns (leading connective, embedded '?', internal temporal connective) to be tested explicitly before a long filler-laden sentence is left completely unsegmented, so latency is not left on the table on sentences with no other visible boundary — while leaving all existing rejection criteria (steps 2-7) unchanged.

next_changelog: Narrowed two over-broad [Never Segment] conditions (blanket discourse-marker restriction and trailing-connective restriction) that were blocking safe, evidence-backed splits: leading connectives (그니까/그래서/근데/etc.) followed by a full subject+predicate clause are now explicitly allowed as segment points right after the marker, and trailing result-connectives (그래서/그러니까) followed by additional clause content may now open a new segment, while bare/contentless trailing connectives remain merged. This follows the critic's 'segment more aggressively' direction by removing prohibitions rather than adding new ones, and targets the dominant under-segmentation failure (leading connectives, trailing short connective clauses) without touching the previously-tried and rejected [When to Segment]/[Decision Procedure] rule additions.

Refreshed [Examples — Segment] to replace two examples that were redundant with the existing terminal-punctuation rule with two new examples illustrating the newly-narrowed rules: splitting after a leading standalone discourse connective when a full clause follows, and splitting before a trailing result-connective clause that carries further content.
